This confirms that the new method (the kd-tree approach) was indeed developed to overcome the specific limitations of reformatting and copying associated with previous structures.

An optimized query method implemented in ISPC that performs $N$ reconstructions and cell/dual-cell queries in parallel using a packet paradigm to traverse the KD-tree [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that an optimized query method implemented in ISPC performs N reconstructions and cell/dual-cell queries in parallel using a packet paradigm to traverse the KD-tree. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in Section 5.3 ('Fast Cell/Dual-Cell Queries'), stating: 'We implemented our reconstruction kernels in ISPC, performing N reconstructions (and correspondingly, N cell/dual cell queries) in parallel... In addition, we implemented cell location in a “packet” paradigm... in which all N queries stay together while going down the tree'. The notes also list this exact sentence as a bullet point.

It references cells by their (float) center point and levels by their (float) center width to utilize floating point units, minimize register pressure, avoid int-to-float conversions, and allow multiply-add capabilities [S1, unofficial].

The claim is explicitly stated in the source text. In the section '5.3 Fast Cell/Dual-Cell Queries', the text reads: 'Rather than operating on logical integer IDs for cells and levels we reference cells by their (float) center point and levels by their (float) center width, which better utilizes floating point units, minimizes register pressure and stack space, avoids costly int-to-float conversions when traversing the data structure, and allows for utilizing modern vector units’ multiply-add capabilities'. This matches the claim word-for-word regarding the method and the reasons provided.
